title: Galaxy SmartTag 3 tanıtıldı: Daha küçük gövde, iPhone desteği ve uzun pil ömrü
summary: Samsung'un yeni konum takip cihazı Galaxy SmartTag 3, daha küçük ve hafif tasarımı, iOS desteği ve 550 güne varan pil ömrüyle duyuruldu.
body:
Samsung, üçüncü nesil bluetooth takip cihazı Galaxy SmartTag 3 modelini resmen duyurdu. Android Police ve The Verge'ün aktardığına göre yeni cihaz, önceki nesle kıyasla yüzde 35 daha küçük bir hacme ve yüzde 33 daha hafif bir gövdeye sahip. Siyah ve beyaz renk seçenekleriyle gelen cihaz, toza ve suya karşı dayanıklılık sunan IP67 sertifikasını koruyor. Tasarımında anahtarlık deliği bulunmayan cihaz için Samsung, farklı aksesuarlar sunacak.

## Gelişmiş takip özellikleri ve iPhone desteği

Galaxy SmartTag 3'ün en dikkat çekici yeniliklerinden biri, Android'in yanı sıra **iOS desteği** de sunması. iPhone kullanıcıları, cihazı kullanabilmek için Samsung’un SmartThings uygulamasını indirebilecek. Cihaz, 900 milyondan fazla Samsung cihazını içeren Galaxy Find Network ağı üzerinden konum takibi yapıyor. Yakın mesafe takibi için ise Ultra-Wideband (UWB) teknolojisinin yanı sıra Bluetooth Channel Sounding kullanılıyor. Cihaz ayrıca normal kullanımda 550 gün, güç tasarrufu modunda ise 790 güne kadar pil ömrü vadediyor.

## Çıkış tarihi ve fiyat belirsizliği

Kaynakların aktardığı bilgilere göre çıkış takvimi konusunda farklı detaylar bulunuyor. Android Police'in haberine göre cihaz küresel pazarda erken Kasım ayında 29,99 dolar fiyat etiketleriyle satışa çıkacak ve dörtlü paketi 99,99 dolar olacak. The Verge ve diğer Android Police haberi ise cihazın **7 Ekim'de** ilk olarak Güney Kore'de raflara çıkacağını, diğer pazarlar için ise 2027 yılının bekleneceğini belirtiyor.

**Neden önemli?** Galaxy SmartTag 3, iOS uyumluluğu ve uzun pil ömrüyle takip cihazı pazarında farklı platform kullanıcılarını buluşturmayı hedefliyor.

source_texts.title: Galaxy SmartTag 3 brings cross-platform functionality to Samsung's best tag yet
source_texts.summary: Samsung's built some excellent smart tags in the past, so we're happy to finally see a revision come up with the Galaxy SmartTag 3. It's smaller, lighter, and offers longer tracking range. Perhaps the biggest news is that this new device will be compatible with both Android and iOS devices.
source_texts.text:
Samsung's built some excellent smart tags in the past, so we're happy to finally see a revision come up with the Galaxy SmartTag 3. It's smaller, lighter, and offers longer tracking range. Perhaps the biggest news is that this new device will be compatible with both Android and iOS devices.
It looks different but it's still distinct
Now, if you want to know how dramatic the physical changes are, Samsung says the volume is about 35% smaller, and the device is 33% lighter than the previous model. We didn't think the previous iteration was bulky at all.
In fact, we like that it stood out from other smart tags on the market, but if Samsung wants to make its new smart tags more compact, we're not complaining about these changes. At least the design still looks unique and elegant, while still offering excellent durability.
Although the SmartTag 3 doesn't have a built-in keyring, the brand will offer accessories so you can easily attach it to bags, luggage, pets, and other items. Despite all the changes, the SmartTag 3 still retains an IP67 rating, protecting it from dust and moisture.
The performance is still there
The Galaxy SmartTag 3 still delivers excellent tracking features. It uses Samsung's Galaxy Find My network to triangulate where the smart tag might be, utilizing over 900 million devices around the world. You get more precise directions with Compass View, backed by Bluetooth Channel Sounding technology, and it also has UWB onboard.
We've seen this on other modern smart tags, and we're glad Samsung is including it on the SmartTag 3. No matter how far you are from the device, you can rely on precise directions once you start getting closer, thanks to these two technologies working in tandem. And just because it's smaller doesn't mean you're not getting the same great battery life as the previous model.
The Galaxy SmartTag 3 offers up to 550 days of battery life under regular use and up to 790 days in Power Saving Mode. Those are some numbers that you can feel confident about.
Some extras
In addition, Samsung provides a feature called Place Notification, which alerts the user when a tagged item enters and leaves a user-defined area. The SmartTag 3 also provides Location History, Movement Detection Alert, and a Left Behind Alert.
Lost Mode helps ensure the SmartTag returns to you if it gets lost, and you can also use the device to trigger routines with compatible smart devices. We know you're excited to get your hands on the SmartTag 3, but it won't be available until sometime in early November.
It will cost $29.99 for one, and a four-pack will cost $99.99. They will be available in two colors: black and white. So, look out for this device come the holiday season.

source_texts.summary: Samsung has announced the SmartTag 3, its latest location tracker , complete with desirable features like Bluetooth Channel Sounding, and the intriguing Place Notification, where you’ll get an alert if the tag moves out of a geo-fenced location.
source_texts.text:
Samsung has announced the SmartTag 3, its latest location tracker, complete with desirable features like Bluetooth Channel Sounding, and the intriguing Place Notification, where you’ll get an alert if the tag moves out of a geo-fenced location.
Smaller and lighter
The SmartTag 3 is 35% smaller and 33% lighter than the SmartTag 2, which was released in 2023, and the revised rounded shape will make it easier to conceal on everything from a keychain to a pet’s collar.
Seeing Bluetooth 6.0 Channel Sounding on the feature list is good news. It enables directional guidance to a tag’s location from about 60 meters away, letting you know when you’re headed in the right direction, and how far away you are.
Ultra-wideband (UWB) is also available when connected to compatible devices, providing even more accurate location data. By using the Galaxy Find Network — consisting of more than 900 million Samsung devices — the SmartTag 3 can be located even when it’s out of range of your phone.
Place Notifications
Finding the tag when it has been lost is a basic requirement, but the SmartTag 3 goes a step further with the Place Notification feature. Here, it tracks the SmartTag 3 in a user-defined geo-fenced area, then sends an alert if it leaves.
The feature also takes advantage of the Galaxy Find Network, and Samsung suggests it will be useful to track pets if they leave your garden, or a bicycle if it unexpectedly leaves its usual parking area.
The SmartTag 3’s location history will be available, as will a movement detection alert, ensuring you stay completely informed about the tag’s activity.
Connectivity upgrades
Samsung has also recognized location tags may want to be used by people who don’t have a Samsung or Android phone, and has added iOS compatibility to the SmartTag 3.
Unfortunately, it’s not through Apple’s Find My service, and iPhone owners will have to download and use Samsung’s SmartThings app. Still, it’s a step in the right direction.
Other features include an NFC-powered Lost Mode, a Left Behind Alert, an IP67 dust and water resistance rating, and a battery that lasts for an impressive 550 days. Activate a Power Saving Mode, and the SmartTag 3’s CR2032 battery can last for up to 790 days.
A long wait for release
The Samsung SmartTag 3 sounds good, but we’re going to have to wait before getting one. It’ll be released in South Korea first, on October 7, but isn’t expected to reach global markets before some time in 2027.
Samsung has not confirmed the price, but we can expect it to be around the same $30 as the SmartTag 2.
If you want a location tracker sooner than 2027, there are many choices. Google recently announced the $30 Pixel Tag, which also has Bluetooth Channel Sounding, plus there are various card-style trackers such as the KeySmart and the Eufy SmartTrack, and recent additions from Chipolo too.

source_texts.text:
Samsung has announced its third-generation Bluetooth tracker, the Galaxy SmartTag 3. It combines a smaller design and improved battery life with a few new tracking and software features, including cross-OS support intended to make it easier to share tracking information with friends and family.
Samsung’s new SmartTag is smaller, longer-lasting, and works with iPhones
The Galaxy SmartTag 3 is launching in South Korea next month, with the rest of the world to follow in 2027.
As revealed by leaks, the SmartTag 3 has adopted a squircle design, similar to the original SmartTag but with one key difference: There’s no cutout for a key ring. That means you’ll have to buy one of Samsung’s protective cases if you want to directly attach the tracker to keys or a carabiner. It has an IP67 rating for protection from the elements.
The new design has benefits though. The SmartTag 3 is 35 percent smaller and 33 percent lighter than the SmartTag 2. It’s 10 percent more power-efficient too, stretching its replaceable CR2032 battery to 550 days of normal use, or 790 days in power-saving mode.
While previous Galaxy SmartTags only worked with Samsung phones, the new generation has been broadened to support iOS too. Samsung doesn’t seem to expect it’s going to win over AirTag owners, but is instead pitching this as a way to share tracking information with friends, family, or dogwalkers for help with finding lost objects or pets. We’ve reached out to Samsung to confirm if other Android phones will be supported too.
New notification alerts can be set to trigger when a SmartTag 3 moves in or out of a set area, movement detection alerts can trigger for smaller shifts, and location history helps you follow a tag’s movements. Tracking is handled by Samsung’s own Galaxy Find Network, rather than Google’s Find Hub, which launched following the release of the SmartTag 2. Once you’re within 200ft of the tracker, ultra-wideband (UWB) and Bluetooth 6.0 Channel Sounding combine on supported phones for more precise detection.
The SmartTag 3 is launching in black and white, but for now, it’s only launching in South Korea, where it goes on sale from October 7th. Samsung says that “additional markets” will follow in 2027, though it hasn’t confirmed a US release or price. The SmartTag 2 cost $29.99, about the same price as Apple’s latest AirTag and Google’s new Pixel Tag.
